# Results

<!-- Generated by `pnpm bench:results` from `baselines/` and `src/harness/results/notes.ts` — edit those, not this file. -->

Where `@codefast/tailwind-variants` actually stands against the field right now, wins and losses given equal weight —
the point of this page is to know where the engine is slower so the next change knows what to aim at. One
machine-derived snapshot, no accreted ledger. The method is in [`BENCH_GUIDE.md`](../di/BENCH_GUIDE.md); re-run it with
the recipe at the bottom.

**This is one full-profile pass, so read the aggregates, not the rows.** GC-exposed for one collection between trials,
one subprocess per scenario, libraries interleaved with rotating order, 3 trials each over the one closure a scenario
builds before its first trial — a single pass measures no between-run variance of its own, 4 of the cells carry a
per-trial IQR above 5%, and 1 cell in 1 row sits above ~30M ops/s, where the ratio moves between runs of the same build
whatever its IQR says. Ratios are worth more than the absolute `hz/op`; a single row is worth less than the group it
sits in. A loss below points at a direction — quote a precise factor only after a paired re-run, except where a loss is
a structural difference that reproduces by construction.

**This page is the baseline.** It is generated from `baselines/2026-10-18T02-39-58-707Z`, whose `observations.jsonl` and
`footprint.json` are committed, so every figure here can be re-read from the repository rather than from a local
`bench-results/` run only the author has. `baselines/` holds that one run and nothing else: the next pass is read
against it, and a pass accepted in its place becomes this page. 28 scenarios ran, 20 of them aggregate-eligible; a `—`
below is a row the library cannot express — `cva` has no slots, no extends and no factory — or a control only codefast
runs, never a row nobody wrote.

**Environment.** `@codefast/tailwind-variants` 0.9.1 on Node 26.1.0 / V8 14.6.202.34-node.19, Apple M3 Max × 14,
darwin/arm64, `--expose-gc --no-warnings` for every library. tailwind-variants 3.3.1 · class-variance-authority 0.7.1.
Each library runs through its default entry with the merge flag passed explicitly, so the two `tv()` libraries differ in
implementation and not in configuration; `cva` has no merge option, so its with-merge rows call `tailwind-merge` after
it, the usual production pairing. Run 2026-10-18, 0 sanity failures. The 1-minute load average read 1.98 as the
subject's child started, on 14 cores.

## This pass

Measured at `ecff22f59` — `@codefast/tailwind-variants` 0.9.1, whose `src` is unchanged since that release, from a
`dist` built first. 15.5s wall, the full profile in isolation, on a machine whose 1-minute load average read under 3 on
14 cores for the whole pass.

**What moved since the previous pass.** Nothing to read against: this is the suite's first committed baseline, so there
is no previous pass and the run diff has no anchor. Every later `pnpm bench:baseline` pass is read against this one.

The harness flags four cells with a per-trial IQR above 5% — `uncached-slots-with-merge`, `uncached-slots-without-merge`
and both sides of `first-render-slots` — and one row above the throughput ceiling, `define-only-slots`. None of them is
in an aggregate: the `uncached-*` rows are codefast-only controls, and the definition rows are declared incomparable.

## Summary — where we stand

Ratios are `@codefast/tailwind-variants ÷ competitor`; above 1× means codefast is faster. Win `>1.03×`, parity
`0.97–1.03×`, loss `<0.97×`. `Comparable` counts the rows both libraries ran, of 20 aggregate-eligible rows codefast
measures; `†` is how many of those the median and geomean carry from above the throughput ceiling — they stay in the
aggregate but no reader should cite one alone.

| Competitor        | Comparable | Win / parity / loss | Median | Geomean |   † |
| ----------------- | ---------: | ------------------: | -----: | ------: | --: |
| tailwind-variants |   20 of 20 |          20 / 0 / 0 |  6.90× |   10.8× |   0 |
| cva               |    4 of 20 |           4 / 0 / 0 |  12.3× |   9.85× |   0 |

**Ahead of every competitor on both aggregates.** tailwind-variants and cva take no row at all.

## What a user waits for

Most rows below price one render of a component with a selection the library has already seen, and many of them run
faster than any frame could notice. Three measurements are the ones an application feels, so they lead: what defining
its components costs as a module loads, what one render costs, and what the library adds to a browser bundle.

**Defining a component.** What a module pays as it loads: one component's `tv()` call, and that definition plus its
first render. `define-only-simple` runs at 27,382,391 ops/s, about 37 ns each, and reads 2.14× tailwind-variants. Beside
it: `define-only-slots` 6.17×† tailwind-variants; `first-render-simple` 1.54× tailwind-variants; `first-render-slots`
1.34×‡ tailwind-variants. An eager library compiles its configuration at definition and a lazy one at the first render,
so the definition and first-render rows are read together, and all four stay off the aggregates. `cva` is not ported to
them.

**One render.** A component rendered with a selection it has seen before, through `tailwind-merge` — what every render
after the first costs. `simple-with-merge` runs at 12,853,801 ops/s, about 78 ns each, and reads 5.88× tailwind-variants
and 6.18× class-variance-authority. Beside it: `complex-with-merge` 15.5× tailwind-variants and 20.1×
class-variance-authority; `slots-with-merge` 4.47× tailwind-variants. Both `tv()` libraries answer a repeated selection
from a cache, so these rows price the hit path; `cva` caches nothing, so its cells compare a hit against a full
computation plus the merge. The `uncached-*` rows in the full table price the miss, on codefast's side alone.

**Bundle.** `pnpm bench:footprint` bundles each library's smallest program — one component with one variant, defined and
rendered once — with Rolldown 1.2.14 for the browser, minified. A library that merges by default ships `tailwind-merge`,
and the merge is measured alone on the last line.

| Library                | Minified | Gzipped |
| ---------------------- | -------: | ------: |
| @codefast/tv           |  39.2 KB | 12.4 KB |
| tailwind-variants      |  40.4 KB | 12.7 KB |
| cva                    |   1.0 KB |  0.6 KB |
| `tailwind-merge` alone |  27.2 KB |  8.5 KB |

`@codefast/tv` ships 12.4 KB gzipped, the second largest of 3 libraries, against a checked-in budget of 12,750 B. Most
of either `tv()` library's share is `tailwind-merge`, which both call by default; `@codefast/tailwind-variants` takes it
as a peer, so an app that already merges its own classes ships one copy. `cva` merges nothing, which is why its
with-merge rows call `tailwind-merge` after it.

## The losses, foregrounded — where to improve

None: no competitor takes a comparable row from codefast in this pass, above the ceiling or below it.

## The wins

Per competitor, its comparable rows and aggregates, its groups from widest to tightest, and every row it does not lose;
the 8 rows declared incomparable stay out of every aggregate.

- **tailwind-variants — 20 of 20 comparable rows, 6.90× median, 10.8× geomean.** By group, widest first: `extreme`
  68.1×, `compound-slots` 33.5×, `extreme-slots` 18.2×, `complex` 15.7×, `extends` 7.10×, `create-tv` 6.69×, `simple`

- **cva — 4 of 4 comparable rows, 12.3× median, 9.85× geomean.** By group, widest first: `complex` 19.2×, `simple`
  5.05×. It takes no row.

## Re-running this

```bash
pnpm bench:baseline            # from benchmarks/tailwind-variants — a full-profile pass, read against the baseline
pnpm bench:report              # derive report.md + report.json from the newest run
pnpm bench:footprint           # the bundle table: each library's smallest program, minified and gzipped
pnpm bench:results             # regenerate this page from baselines/
```

Accepting a pass replaces the one run under `baselines/` with it: move the new run's `observations.jsonl` there in place
of the old directory, run `pnpm bench:footprint --save` to record the bundle table beside it, and write its `notes.md` —
the commit it measured and what moved since the previous pass, with the paired A/B behind any row the pass flags. Then
`pnpm bench:results` rebuilds this page; it refuses to build while a note in `src/harness/results/notes.ts` names a row
that no longer loses, while a loss below the ceiling has no note, or while a note carries a figure. CI runs
`pnpm bench:results --check`, so the page cannot drift from the baseline it names.

Before quoting any single loss as a factor rather than a direction, re-measure it paired and alternating on a quiet
machine — a full pass carries no between-run variance of its own. The A/B protocol is in
[`BENCH_GUIDE.md`](../di/BENCH_GUIDE.md): `pnpm bench:ab` swaps the change's `src` per side, narrowed to the target rows
plus warm canaries, and reads the per-trial spread, not one ratio. `pnpm bench:list` prints which rows each library
implements.
